rules.title: Unsuffixed integer literal dispatches to any integer param it fits
rules.statement: For overload/call dispatch an argument that is an UNSUFFIXED integer literal is compatible with an integer parameter type P iff its value fits P; a SUFFIXED literal (e.g. `9u64`) has a concrete type and must match by type, not by value. The flex path excludes Enum params (P!=Enum) so an integer never reinterprets enum by-pointer storage.
examples: push(9u64) // matches push(i64)? NO — u64 only

rules.title: Integer expression widening to target type
rules.statement: An integer-typed expression e is implicitly widened to a target integer type T (via an inserted cast) iff can_widen(kind(e),T) holds, OR e is an integer literal whose value fits T. Otherwise no implicit widening occurs.

rules.title: &<int-literal> sizes its temporary to the expected pointee width
rules.statement: When `&L` (an address-of an integer literal materialized as a temporary) is passed where `&T`/`&mut T` is expected and T is a wider integer type that L can widen to or fits, the inner literal is cast to T before being addressed, so the temporary's storage slot is sized to T (preventing a narrow temp read as the wider pointee).

rules.title: Writ view container recognition
rules.statement: A type t (optionally behind one &/&mut) denotes a Writ value iff its underlying Struct/ZonedStruct name is one of {Writ, WritView, WritStatic, Rc} (Rc being the `Rc<Writ>` runtime container). One level of reference is peeled before matching.
rules.uncertainty: Matches by struct name only; does not check Rc's type argument is Writ.

rules.title: let-chain desugars to nested if-let with duplicated else
rules.statement: A let-chain (`if a && let P = e && b { .. } else { .. }`) desugars to nested `if let`/`if` over the segment list, with the ELSE branch textually duplicated at every fall-through site (matching Rust's classic desugar); user-visible side effects in ELSE are duplicated.
rules.divergence: Accepted limitation: ELSE side effects duplicated per fall-through site.

rules.title: Or-pattern inside a variant payload distributes into one arm per alternative
rules.statement: A multi-alternative or-pattern appearing as a variant payload arg (`Some(P|Q)`) is fanned out into one effective arm per alternative (`Some(P) | Some(Q)`); each re-evaluates the arm guard with its own bindings, so a failing guard backtracks to the next alternative.

rules.title: Nested enum-payload exhaustiveness checked on AST patterns
rules.statement: Exhaustiveness for nested enum-payload patterns (`Some(Some(v))`/`Some(None)`/`None`) is decided over the original AST patterns, descending into each variant's single payload, because the LIR-level check skips guarded (desugared) arms.

rules.title: Droppable auto-ref'd method receiver temporary lives to end of statement
rules.statement: When a droppable rvalue is auto-referenced as a `&self`/`&mut self` method receiver (`W::mk(..).get()`), the materialized temporary lives until the end of the enclosing statement and is then dropped (Rust temporary-scope semantics), via hoisting into a statement-scoped `let` whose scope-exit runs the destructor; the hoisted `let` is `let mut` when the receiver is `&mut self`.

rules.title: Return-value temporaries drop before the return terminator
rules.statement: When lowering a `return <value>` whose value materialized statement-temporaries, the value is pre-bound to a local and the temporaries are dropped before the `return` terminator (`let __t..; let __rv = value; drop __t..; return __rv;`) so the drops are not dead code after the terminator.

rules.title: Generic Deref/DerefMut autoderef lowers as a method call
rules.statement: Autoderef of a receiver whose type implements Deref/DerefMut — including a generic impl (Box/Rc/Arc) whose `deref` is not a concrete symbol at sema time — is emitted as a `deref()`/`deref_mut()` method call (monomorphized later), and the resulting Target place type is obtained by substituting the Deref impl's target pattern against the receiver type.

rules.title: T::CONST on an abstract type-param lowers to a per-impl accessor call
rules.statement: `T::CONST` where T is an abstract type-param bound by a trait declaring `const CONST` lowers to a zero-arg accessor call `T__kassoc_CONST()`; monomorphization rewrites `T__` to the concrete type and the per-impl accessor supplies the value.

rules.title: Untyped closure literal infers parameter types from an Fn-family bound
rules.statement: An untyped closure literal (`|x| ..`) appearing where an Fn-family-bounded type-param is expected infers its parameter types from the bound's signature, after the active substitution is applied; peeling through Ref/MutRef/Ptr and single-type-arg wrappers (`Box<dyn Fn(..)>`) to expose the inner callable type.

rules.title: Associated-type lookup keyed by trait type-args when ambiguous
rules.statement: Associated-type resolution for two distinct `Trait<T>` impls of one target type is disambiguated by a `$G<n>$<a1>$..` suffix encoding the concrete trait type-args, preferring the suffixed key when args are known from the current impl context and falling back to the plain key for single/non-generic-trait impls.
